Earlier, we spoke about the disjoined letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) at the beginnings of some surahs of the Qur'an, and that they have a wisdom intended by the Truthful, glorified is He. We hover around it, and then we say: God knows best what He intends.

The waw here is for conjunction. That is, ﴿Ḥā Mīm. By the Clear Book﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 1-2] are one and the same thing, and both are the Qur'an, by which Allah swears. But He separated them by the conjunction, because ﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 1] we recite and believe in, without knowing its meaning, rather we refer it back to the One who spoke it, glory be to Him. As for ﴿the Clear Book﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 2], that is: the evident, manifest one that makes things clear, so we understand it and know its meanings.

This is the statement of what is sworn to. Almighty God swears by these Arabic letters, and by the Book composed of these letters, that He made it ﴿an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 3]. He called it a Book (kitab) because it is written in lines, and a Qur'an because it is recited, and He described it as Arabic to emphasise that it was revealed in the language of the people, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make [the message] clear for them...﴾ [Ibrahim: 4].

Therefore, it is necessary that the Messenger be in the language of his people so that they may understand him and the process of conveying the message may be completed. If you say: how then was Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent to all people of differing languages?

We say: He was sent in the language of his people, those who were contemporaries of him and who directly received his first instructions. When they understood them, were convinced, and believed in their truth, they carried them to other nations, and they travelled with them throughout the earth in movement, action, conduct and application.

This is the meaning of the message to mankind as a whole: its miraculous quality lies in practical conduct and application. For this reason history tells us that Islam spread across the lands through the upright conduct that dazzled all people, so they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. Read: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ [Fussilat: 33].

And He, glory be to Him, says of this Ummah: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. Thus were all the successors charged with carrying this message: the Messenger testifies that he conveyed to us, and the other nations testify that we conveyed to them.

Therefore, through the language this Ummah understood this method and translated it into action; it was transformed from an unlettered, ignorant nation with no order and no law into a refined nation that attracted the most advanced nations of the earth, such as Persia in the east and Rome in the west. They shook these two civilisations when they applied the teachings of the method that Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, brought to them. This is what drew attention to Islam.

Thus, when we reflect on the surah of our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, we find this practical, applied model of faith. Read: ﴿And there entered with him into prison two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine," and the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying on my head bread, from which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good."﴾ [Yusuf: 36].

Yusuf attained this rank and became the object of those who asked, and why? Because he reached the level of ihsan (excellence), which is the summit of practical application of the method he brought. Then he himself explains this practical path that brought him to the rank of interpretation, saying: ﴿He said, "No food will come to you as provision but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and are in the Hereafter disbelievers. And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind, but most of mankind do not show gratitude."﴾ [Yusuf: 37-38].

That is: if you did as I did, you would become able to understand dreams and interpret them exactly as I do.

This practical path is itself what enabled our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, to seize the opportunity to carry out his missionary task. Before giving the two questioners what they wanted, he gave them what he himself wanted first, the call to Allah, while they were in need of him and listening to every word he said.

Therefore we see him hasten to this summary of faith and creed, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison, are many scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer? What you worship other than Him are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Judgment is only for Allah. He has commanded that you not worship except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.﴾ [Yusuf: 39-40] Then after that he explains the dream to them.

Thus: the conduct of Yusuf is what drew attention to him, and likewise true, upright conduct in every time and place is what draws attention to you and attracts hearts.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 4:

God's words: ﴿And indeed it﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4], i.e., the Clear Book whose description has preceded, which is the Noble Qur'an. ﴿In the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]. The Mother of the Book means the original Book, or the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), from which all the revelations of heaven were taken, and in which all events were recorded. ﴿With Us﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4], meaning: with Allah. That is, it has not been given to anyone, and this means that it is guarded and preserved.

﴿Indeed, it is sublime﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4], i.e., in its essence. Al-'uluww (sublimity) means elevation, because it is the Book that seals all the revelations before it and is dominant (muhaymin) over them.

The dominance (haymanah) of the Qur'an over the earlier books is that it agrees with them in the fundamental articles of belief, the acts of worship and morals, and then it abrogated from the revelations what is not suitable for the age, and it shook off the corruption that had befallen them of alteration, change, or distortion (tahrif).

The Qur'an has related about them that they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of, and what they did not forget they concealed, and what they did not conceal they distorted. Moreover, they added to all of that and did not stop at the limit of distortion; rather, they brought words from themselves and said: "It is from Allah." Recite: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah"...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79].

This is the dominance of the Qur'an over what preceded it of books, and its sublimity over them.

As for His words ﴿the Wise﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4]: al-Hakim (the Wise) is the one who places a thing in its proper place with respect to its time and its suitable place, so you see everything in it well-regulated. The Qur'an is the Book with which the heavenly books were sealed, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Seal of all the Messengers.

If you say: Why does the Truth, glorified is He, preserve His speech in the Mother of the Book, when He does not err or forget, and His knowledge encompasses everything, and nothing is hidden from Him?

They said: Allah, exalted is He, preserved His speech in the Mother of the Book for the sake of the angels. When they see the Preserved Tablet, they find in it ancient speech which the events and the conduct of people in the universe confirm, and reality comes in accordance with what the Truth has informed of in His speech, so they increase in love for Allah and care for Him, and they judge that Allah is the All-Knowing, the Wise.

This is the secret of writing, because the angels had earlier said regarding the creation of man: ﴿They said, "Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30].

Some of them said that the "Mother of the Book" in ﴿the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4] is not the Preserved Tablet, on the basis of His words about the Qur'an: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise (muhkamat), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous (mutashabihat)...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 7]. So "the Mother of the Book" here means: the precise verses (al-ayat al-muhkamat). Perhaps in this meaning there is an alert to us that this surah (al-Zukhruf) is among the precise verses, with not one verse of it among the ambiguous ones.

The Messenger (ﷺ) has also clarified for us the ruling on the precise (muhkam) and the ambiguous (mutashabih), and he said: Allah, exalted is He, said regarding the ambiguous: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 7], and we stop; then ﴿And those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 7]. Therefore: we act upon the precise and believe in the ambiguous.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 5:

The hamza here carries the meaning of a rebuking interrogative (istifham inkari), and the meaning of ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ﴾ is: shall we leave off? One says: "ḍaraba 'an al-'amal" and "aḍraba 'an al-'amal," meaning: he left the work and abstained from it. From this comes: "Al-'ummal aḍraba 'an al-'amal" (the workers went on strike).

So the Truth says to them: Shall We abandon your admonition, turn away from you and leave you thus neglected (hamalan), because you have been excessive against your own souls, have denied the Reminder and disbelieved in it?

No indeed. We will continue to send you admonition and clarification, and We will hold you to proof and evidence. If you do not believe through the proof and do not accept it, then the turn of raiding, conquest and victory over you comes, until you believe. This is a mercy from God toward them, since they are His servants and His creation, and He wills their salvation; He is more merciful to them than a mother is to her child, even while they are disbelievers in Him.

Had He left them to what they wished, they would have persisted in their corruption and deserved destruction and punishment. The disbeliever, when he believes, God shows him mercy through faith, and God shows mercy to society from his evil and corruption if he remains in his disbelief. Thus the Reminder, meaning here the Revelation, is a mercy from God and a good which He sends down to His servants out of mercy toward them.

Therefore they said: "If you have an enemy, do not invoke destruction upon him; rather, pray for his guidance, for you do not benefit from his destruction; rather, you benefit from his conduct, and his good returns to you if he is guided. The fruits of good benefit the whole society. From this standpoint, Islam forbade us from concealing knowledge, for when you conceal knowledge you deprive your society of its good; when you teach others you benefit from their good and are safe from their evil."

So then: among God's mercy toward them is that He continues the sending down of the Qur'an to them despite their obstinacy, their disbelief and their persistence in error. And indeed, with the passage of time and the succession of the revelation, the chieftains of disbelief embraced Islam one after another: 'Umar embraced Islam, 'Amr, Khalid, 'Ikrima and many others.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says to them: You are in need of reading history and taking a lesson from the procession of the messages, that you may see the end of those who denied the messengers. The history of the messages affirms the victory of God's messengers over those who denied them, because this is God's custom regarding the messengers: that God gives them victory in the end, and that the final outcome is theirs over their deniers. God seizes them according to the measure of their denial: ﴿فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنبِهِ﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40] ("So each We seized for his sin").

And the Truth, glorified is He, has addressed them with His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ * وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138] ("And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night; will you not then reason?"), meaning: the matter is not a theoretical speech; rather, it is a lived and witnessed reality that you must reason about and learn the lesson from, lest there descend upon you punishment like what descended upon them.

Here "kam" (how many) indicates abundance: ﴿and how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 6], that is, among the earlier nations, those who used to deny the messengers and mock them.

Here "kam" (how many) indicates abundance: ﴿and how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 6], that is, among the earlier nations, those who used to deny the messengers and mock them.

Meaning: O disbelievers of Quraysh, take a lesson from the earlier nations whom Allah destroyed, who were stronger than you, yet their strength did not protect them and did not repel the punishment of Allah. ﴿And the example of the former peoples has passed on﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 8], meaning their story and what befell them, because this is the promise of Allah to the messengers. ﴿And certainly has Our word preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant﴾ [as-Saffat: 171-173]. So you must find the outcome of this denial: either you will be defeated in this world, or the punishment will be stored up for you in the Hereafter.

Divine Lord (al-Haqq) wishes to show them that they deny the Messenger of God and oppose his call out of arrogance and obstinacy, without relying on the logic of reason and wisdom. He takes this truth and establishes it from their own tongues: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9].

In another place: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah..."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87]. This is a truth they do not deny and acknowledge, because the matter of creation is one that no one has claimed for himself, and no rival has stood up to it.

First, it is strange of them that they believe that Allah is the Creator, and that He is Almighty and All-Knowing, and yet they take this obstinate stance towards the Messenger of God. Then why did they not say, for example, "He created them, Allah," since He has no rival, and instead describe the Divine Lord as "the Almighty, the All-Knowing"? They said: because they followed the ways of their fathers and thought them the best, so they said: ﴿Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers upon...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170]. Thus this kept them from following the truth.

The meaning of ﴿al-'Azīz﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9] is: the Victorious who cannot be overcome. So they have refuted themselves, for whatever they do, they must be overcome.

Their saying in describing the Divine Lord, ﴿al-'Azīz al-'Alīm﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9], is in the manner of a speaker who may add from his own part what was not conveyed to him, as if you sent a person with a message and said to him: "Go to so-and-so," just like that, without titles and without descriptions, and say to him such-and-such.

So when the messenger goes, he says: "By God, so-and-so told me, 'Go to Sheikh so-and-so, or Master so-and-so, and say to him such-and-such,'" adding the description from himself. Likewise, these people say ﴿created them, the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9], because they know that God, exalted is He, is Almighty and All-Knowing.

Then He, glorified is He, wished to show them His power and His knowledge, so He said: ﴿He who made the earth for you a cradle...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 10]. The word mahd (cradle) originally means the spread bedding in which a child rests, whether sitting or sleeping, and from it we say a "mumahhad" road, meaning prepared and levelled so as to ease the one who walks upon it.

So the Truth likens us to children, and a child cannot prepare for himself, so if Allah had not prepared the earth for us, we would not have been able to prepare it.

﴿And made for you therein roads...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 10], meaning: paths that you travel and move along from one place to another, because the interests of creation require moving from their place of residence to the places of their interests, ﴿that you may be guided﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 10], meaning: in your journeys to your interests and purposes.

When the Divine Lord bestows His favours upon them, He does so only to soften their hearts and draw them to His presence, so that they may be guided to Him, believe in Him, and affirm His Messenger.

...When the Truth, glory be to Him, bestows upon them some of His blessings, He does so only to soften their hearts and draw them toward His presence, so that perhaps they may be guided to Him, believe in Him, and affirm His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 11:

His saying ﴿from the sky﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 11], meaning: from the direction of the sky, ﴿in a measure﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 11], with a specific reckoning and a determined quantity, according to what the wisdom of God requires, such that we benefit from this water and give life to the earth by it without harms, because water may be a means of destruction and ruin, as we have seen in the story of our master Noah.

Therefore the descent of water is restricted here by His saying ﴿in a measure﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 11], meaning: according to your need and according to what sets you right. For this reason our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), taught us to say when the rain falls. The meaning of ﴿then We give life thereby to a dead land﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 11] is: We gave it life with vegetation, as He, glory be to Him, said in another place: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind of pair﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

So the dead land, which has no vegetation in it, is why in jurisprudence you find the chapter on reviving dead land (iḥyā' al-mawāt), and in the noble hadith the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: [...]

This is a principle which, if the states of the world adopted it, we would have eliminated poverty, goodness would have spread over every corner of the earth, and we would not have found a single span of desert.

And in Egypt we have a clear example: when the government restricted the people and prevented their spreading into the desert, the people crowded into the valley and the Delta, and want occurred, and we were not able to secure self-sufficiency in agricultural produce.

And when the state permitted the cultivation of the desert and encouraged the people to it, what happened? We saw the desert turn green and bring forth for us what is delicious and good of vegetables and fruit, and whoever travels the desert road sees that.

God, glory be to Him, has also made clear that water descends from the sky so that people benefit from it in cultivating the land, and what exceeds their need is absorbed by the earth until rivers form beneath the surface of the earth. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and then makes it flow as springs in the earth...﴾ [al-Zumar: 21].

The word (mayyitan) with a sukun (mayt) means: that over which death has actually occurred. As for mayyit with the shadda, it is what is judged to be dead even if it is still alive.

And you ask me about the explanation of mayt and mayyit, so here it is for you, if you understand: I have explained it.

Whoever has a soul, that one is mayyit, and the mayt is only one who is carried to the grave.

Among this is His saying, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [al-Zumar: 30].

And the poet said in praise of our master, the Messenger of God:

Your brother Jesus called a dead one and it stood up for him, and you have revived generations from non-existence.

And His saying: ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 11]. "Thus" means: just as We give life to the dead land, We will give life to you and bring you forth from your graves. So take from what you witness in the earth as evidence for what is hidden from you of matters of resurrection and the revival of the dead. When We tell you that God gives you life after your death, then believe.

The word ﴿al-azwāj﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 12] is the plural of zawj. As we have said, a zawj is a single thing that has a counterpart like it, and a zawjān is each of two opposites, such as white and black, sweet and sour, above and below, right and left.

Zawjiyyah (pairedness), as Allah the Most High has informed us, exists in everything: ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49]. Some of these pairs we know and some we do not know. Therefore He said here, ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 12]. The word ﴿kullahā﴾ ("all of them") means: both what we know, such as male and female, and what we do not know.

People of reflection and contemplation pause at this verse, seeking the wisdom in it. Allah the Most High bestows favour by creating all pairs in order to establish for us that He, glory be to Him, is the One (fard) with no pair alongside Him. The rule of scientific exhaustive enumeration says: the zawj means two, or that which is divisible by two.

When we take the sequence of numbers from its beginning, we say: one is the single thing that has no second, and two means one to which another one has been joined.

So: two, as a number, needs one, whereas one needs nothing. Therefore the true single (al-fard al-haqq) is the One who needs nothing, and this belongs only to Allah, mighty and majestic.

So: the pair needs the single, and the single does not need the pair.

Since He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of all pairs, He is therefore the One who has no like. The one who reflects finds that the two members of a pair differ in attributes, such as male and female; each has its own attributes, along with shared attributes between them.

The shared attributes mean that each member of the pair has a likeness (mithl) to the other, and the differing attributes mean that each one has a deficiency relative to the other. Allah, the Most High, is the One who has no likeness, and the Perfect in whom there is no deficiency. It is as if the verse establishes that Allah, the Most High, is the Single Creator who needs nothing, while everything needs Him.

As for His saying: ﴿And He made for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 12]: al-fulk means the ships. Among the cattle that are ridden is the camel, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves﴾ [An-Nahl: 7].

The meaning is: He created for you, from the ships and the cattle, that which you ride. But He said ﴿mā tarkabūn﴾ ("that which you ride") and did not say "that you ride in them," so that the ships would be subsumed under the cattle. We do not ride ships; rather, we ride in them. For this reason He named them ﴿al-fulk al-mashḥūn﴾ [As-Saffat: 140] and said: ﴿until when you are in the ships﴾ [Yunus: 22].

So: we ride upon the cattle and mount their backs, and we ride in ships. Even the ancient ships had walls and seats inside them, so how much more so the ships made of decks like houses, which the Qur'an described as being like mountains.

But why did He give precedence to the cattle and subsume the ships within them? There must be a wisdom here, because it is Allah, the Most High, who is speaking. Therefore you find every word in its place with precise expressive exactness. He gave precedence to the cattle and said ﴿mā tarkabūn﴾ because we mount upon the cattle, whereas for ships it is "in" them.

Moreover, cattle are the direct creation of Allah, whereas ships are the creation of man. And Allah, the Most High, addresses with this verse primarily the Arabs, and the Arabs had no knowledge of ships and did not ride them; rather, their means of transport and carrying were the cattle, which were familiar to them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verses 13–14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13]. Al-istiwa' (sitting firmly, settling comfortably) here indicates rest. After you were walking and bearing the hardship of the journey, you mounted an animal made subservient to you. Therefore He asks you to remember that this is a blessing from Allah upon you, which requires your gratitude and remembrance of Him, and to beware of heedlessness of the remembrance of blessings and the thanking of the Benefactor. The animal carries you on four legs, which makes it smooth and easy to travel on for you.

Ships in their sailing need three elements: the ship, the sea in which it travels, and the wind that moves it. So whenever it carries you, remember all these blessings that have come together to carry you wherever you wish.

Then our Lord, mighty and majestic, teaches us the appropriate way of remembering this blessing, which is to say, as it came in the Qur'an: ﴿Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that [ourselves]﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13].

The Prophet (ﷺ) taught us the supplication for travel and mounting, and taught us to mention Allah when we begin a new task. Therefore, concerning the story of the ship, He said: ﴿In the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring...﴾ [Hud: 41]. The remembrance of Allah is the energy from which we draw help, the strength for travelling or for performing work.

When you recite the supplication for mounting and say, "Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that," you are in fact negating vanity from yourself and acknowledging that you ride this vessel not by your own power over it, but by the power of Allah who made it easy for you and subjected it to serve you. Were it not that Allah subjected it, you would not have been able to control it or mount its back.

The ship may sink with those on board, and the animal may die under you in the middle of the road. So: always remember Allah's power in this matter, and hasten to mention Allah when mounting.

As for these animals you ride and carry upon, do you have any merit in them? Even ships, which are the handiwork of your hand, had man not known them unless Allah taught Noah the craft of shipbuilding: ﴿And We carried him upon [a vessel] of planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar: 13], and He said: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration...﴾ [Hud: 37]. So the first idea in it is from Allah, mighty and majestic.

Remember that the horse you ride and the camel you carry upon are stronger than you, and if it becomes stubborn you cannot control it. Therefore, the Exalted said concerning these animals: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71–72]. Had Allah not made them subservient, we would not have been able to subdue them.

We have already said: a small child leads the camel, mounts it, and makes it kneel, and the camel obeys him with ease and facility. Indeed, it is a sight that calls you to reflect on the power of Allah who subjected this huge creature to serve this small child who can do nothing.

On the other hand, you find, for example, the flea that disturbs your rest and troubles you all night, and you cannot do anything to it. Why? Because the Creator, glory be to Him, subjected this to you and did not subject that to you. So reflect, and do not think that you ride these vehicles by your own strength or by your own capability over them.

The meaning of ﴿And we were not capable of that﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13] is: unable to master it or overpower it; that is, we have no power over it, no control, and no dominion except through Allah's subjecting it to us. ﴿And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 14], that is: we will go back and return.

The animal carries you on four legs, which makes it smooth and easy to travel on for you.

Ships in their sailing need three elements: the ship, the sea in which it travels, and the wind that moves it. So whenever it carries you, remember all these blessings that have come together to carry you wherever you wish.

Then our Lord, mighty and majestic, teaches us the appropriate way of remembering this blessing, which is to say, as it came in the Qur'an: ﴿Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that [ourselves]﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13].

The Prophet (ﷺ) taught us the supplication for travel and mounting, and taught us to mention Allah when we begin a new task. Therefore, concerning the story of the ship, He said: ﴿In the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring...﴾ [Hud: 41]. The remembrance of Allah is the energy from which we draw help, the strength for travelling or for performing work.

When you recite the supplication for mounting and say, "Glory be to He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that," you are in fact negating vanity from yourself and acknowledging that you ride this vessel not by your own power over it, but by the power of Allah who made it easy for you and subjected it to serve you. Were it not that Allah subjected it, you would not have been able to control it or mount its back.

The ship may sink with those on board, and the animal may die under you in the middle of the road. So: always remember Allah's power in this matter, and hasten to mention Allah when mounting.

As for these animals you ride and carry upon, do you have any merit in them? Even ships, which are the handiwork of your hand, had man not known them unless Allah taught Noah the craft of shipbuilding: ﴿And We carried him upon [a vessel] of planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar: 13], and He said: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration...﴾ [Hud: 37]. So the first idea in it is from Allah, mighty and majestic.

Remember that the horse you ride and the camel you carry upon are stronger than you, and if it becomes stubborn you cannot control it. Therefore, the Exalted said concerning these animals: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71–72]. Had Allah not made them subservient, we would not have been able to subdue them.

We have already said: a small child leads the camel, mounts it, and makes it kneel, and the camel obeys him with ease and facility. Indeed, it is a sight that calls you to reflect on the power of Allah who subjected this huge creature to serve this small child who can do nothing.

On the other hand, you find, for example, the flea that disturbs your rest and troubles you all night, and you cannot do anything to it. Why? Because the Creator, glory be to Him, subjected this to you and did not subject that to you. So reflect, and do not think that you ride these vehicles by your own strength or by your own capability over them.

The meaning of ﴿And we were not capable of that﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13] is: unable to master it or overpower it; that is, we have no power over it, no control, and no dominion except through Allah's subjecting it to us. ﴿And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 14], that is: we will go back and return.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 15:

His saying, glorified is He, ﴿And they have attributed to Him from among His servants a portion﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 15] is a reference to those who attributed offspring to Allah, exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. That is because the offspring is a part of its father. In the noble hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "She is a piece of me" (i.e., a part of me).

When they attributed offspring to Allah the Exalted, at one time they named Him "the son of Allah," at another time they said "Allah," and at another time they said "the third of three." What is astonishing is that they fell into this error with whom? With the Prophet whom Allah sent to them. They made the Prophet himself a means to shirk.

The second matter: the part that separates from the two parents is either male or female, and it is known that the male is, in their view, more honourable than the female and preferred over her, as evidenced by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed grief. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that which he has been given the good news of...﴾ [An-Nahl: 58-59].

And these people, when they attributed offspring to Allah the Exalted, attributed females to Him, and she is blameworthy in their eyes. You know the story of Abu Hamzah, when he married a woman who did not bear a male child, so he abandoned her for another, and she said, venting her feelings:

What is wrong with Abu Hamzah that he does not come to us,
He stays in the house that is nearest to us, angry,
Does he not know that bearing sons is not in our hands? By Allah, that is not in our hands,
So we are like the earth for those who plant, we give what they sow within us.

Thus the Arab woman of old declared what modern science has established: that the woman is not responsible for the maleness or femaleness of the child; she is only a receiver and a carrier, while the man is the one responsible for this matter.

The Qur'an says: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female, from a drop when it is emitted﴾ [An-Najm: 45-46]. The "nutfah" (drop) is the water of the man which fertilises the ovum and determines maleness and femaleness.

Because attributing offspring to Allah the Exalted is a great and grievous matter, the verse is concluded with His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 15]. Reflect on the precision of the expression here, which suits the gravity of the accusation: "inna" (indeed) is for emphasis, and "lakafur" (ungrateful) is an intensive form of "kafir" (disbelieving). "Mubin" (clear) means manifestly and evidently disbelieving, so his disbelief is hidden from no one.

Allah, glory be to Him, responds to them with this interrogative which conveys astonishment: ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 16]. That is to say: Is it conceivable, when He is the Creator, that He would choose sons for you, who are the superior kind, while reserving for Himself daughters, who are the inferior kind?

In another place He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues describe the lie that for them is the best. Undoubtedly, for them is the Fire, and they will be hastened into it [neglected]﴾ [An-Nahl: 62].

Then Allah, glory be to Him, gives us the proof of their lying and their fabrication against Him: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 17:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When one of them is given news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17] is a metaphor (kinayah) for the daughters whom they attributed to Allah and made a likeness to Him, glorified is He. This is because the child, as we have said, is a likeness of its father and a part of him, while they, at the same time, attribute daughters to Allah, yet they dislike them, and the face of the man among them darkens when he is given the good news of a daughter.

﴿And he is inwardly distressed﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 17], meaning: he is filled with rage, vexation and grief.

So, how can you attribute to Allah that which you would not accept for yourselves? For this reason the Qur'an described this matter as an unjust and oppressive division, and the Exalted said in Surah An-Najm: ﴿Is it for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [An-Najm: 21-22].

He chose this unusual word, which does not occur in the Qur'an except once, so that the strangeness of the word would indicate the strangeness of the saying they uttered.

Also here the alif is an interrogative particle. God, glory be to Him, says: "Is one who is brought up amid ornaments, and who is unclear when it comes to argument, [equal to one who is not]?" The meaning of ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornament﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 18] is: raised in adornment and luxury. Thus among us, for example, we take care of a girl's clothing and appearance, and we dress her in earrings, bracelets and beautiful garments, unlike a boy.

﴿And who, in contention...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 18] means: in situations of dispute and defence, ﴿is unclear﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 18], meaning: he has no strength in making his proof clear.

So the daughter they attributed to God is raised in luxury and ease, wearing silk and gold and adornment, because she was created to attract. We are keen on a girl's appearance and form, and we adorn her first and last, so that she may marry.

Generally we resort to adornment and artificial beauty when a girl does not have natural beauty. This is shown by the fact that the Arabs used to call a beautiful woman *ghaniyah* (one who is self-sufficient), meaning that she has become independent of any adornment through her natural beauty.

As for the male, it is the opposite: the boy goes with his father to the field and the factory, into disputes and arguments, and into every hard labour. So are the two equal?

This does not mean that this is a general rule for the whole sex. We may find among women one who has sound opinion and strong argument, who surpasses men. You remember that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions were prevented from entering Makkah for the 'Umrah, while they were on its outskirts, the Messenger of God was compelled to conclude the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah with the disbelievers of Makkah, that he would return this year and perform the pilgrimage in the year that follows.

When the Companions became angry and rose up, and it was grievous to them to be barred from the House while they were at the outskirts of Makkah, even 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) rose up and said: "O Messenger of God, are we not upon the truth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Are they not upon falsehood?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then why should we give a humiliation in our religion?"

The people began to disobey the Messenger of God and defy his commands, until he entered his tent, where Umm Salamah was, while he was angry. She said to him: "What is the matter, O Messenger of God, that I see you angry?" He said: "The people have perished. I commanded them and they did not comply."

She said: "O Messenger of God, excuse them, for they are a distressed people. They came from Madinah longing for the House, and it is hard for them to be barred from it while they are at the outskirts of Makkah. So go, O Messenger of God, to what God has commanded you, and do it before them. If they see you doing it, they will know that the matter is a firm decree with no room for dispute." So when the Messenger did it before them, they did likewise, the problem ended, and they returned to Madinah.

Out of mercy for the zeal of the Muslims for their religion, revelation came down upon our master the Messenger of God while he was on the road, before they reached Madinah, clarifying for them the divine wisdom behind their returning this year. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering detained from reaching its place of sacrifice. Had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby incur a liability without knowledge, [He would have permitted you to attack]—that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills. Had they been separated, We would have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment﴾ [al-Fath: 25].

So the wisdom in returning this year is that there were many Muslims in Makkah who had concealed their Islam. Had you entered Makkah by force, and fighting had broken out between you and the disbelievers, your Muslim brothers would have been struck, and you would have harmed them without knowing it. Thus they recognised the correctness of the Messenger of God's opinion, and that he (ﷺ) was upon the truth.

This is an example of sound judgement among women. History is full of examples of women who surpassed men in argument, strength and soundness of opinion, because the Creator, glory be to Him, does not create mechanically, but by power and wisdom. It is not a requirement that all men have strength in argument while all women have weakness of opinion and inability to argue. A rule must have exceptions.

If the rule concerning women is ﴿one who is brought up in ornament, and who is unclear in contention﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 18], then God's absolute power turns this weakness into a strength that surpasses the strength of men. We see among women one who was a queen over her people, such as the Queen of Sheba, whose story the Qur'an recounts with Prophet Sulayman (Solomon).

Did she attain sovereignty because there were no men? Not at all. She surpassed them through her intelligence and the strength of her opinion, until men submitted to her and placed her ahead of them.

When we read her story in Surah al-Naml we find what indicates this intelligence, this shrewdness, this political skill and this ability in argument. When the hoopoe described her, he said: ﴿I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she has a great throne﴾ [al-Naml: 23].

When Sulayman's letter reached her, she did not monopolise the decision, but consulted the notables: ﴿She said: "O chiefs, a noble letter has been delivered to me"﴾ [al-Naml: 29], and she adopted the principle of consultation (shura): ﴿She said: "O chiefs, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you bear witness"﴾ [al-Naml: 32].

Then she tried to resolve the matter in a gentle way, far from violence and bloodshed, because she knew the nature of kings: ﴿She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it and make its honoured people abased. And thus do they act. * And indeed I am going to send them a gift and see with what the envoys return"﴾ [al-Naml: 34–35].

Observe her tact and her political skill in her reply when they disguised her throne and asked her: ﴿Is your throne like this?﴾ [al-Naml: 42]? ﴿She said: "It is as if it were it"﴾ [al-Naml: 42]. When the matter ended with her Islam, she said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Naml: 44]. She did not become Muslim out of fear of Sulayman, nor to please him; rather she submitted with him to God. So I and he are equal in submitting our faces to God, exalted is He.

In our country, Egypt, there is (Shajar al-Durr), who had sound opinion and political wisdom that enabled her to get past the crisis when her husband died. She concealed the news of his death and herself directed the affairs of rule, so that the army, which was outside the country on a military mission, would not be weakened. Shajar al-Durr is the one who connected us with the Ka'bah, and she who clothed it, and she was a woman.

These examples are not only from Islamic history. In the pre-Islamic era too we find prominent women who had an opinion and wisdom surpassing men.

It is related that Umamah bint al-Harith ibn 'Amr married 'Awf ibn Muhallim al-Shaybani, and bore him a daughter named Umm Unas. She was beautiful, and the Arabs heard of her beauty and eloquence. 'Amr ibn Hujr, the prince of Kindah, who was one of the leaders of the Arabs, wished to marry her.

'Amr said to his companion Ibn Sinan: "What do you think, O Ibn Sinan? If I proposed to any tribe of the Arabs, would they reject me?" He said: "Yes. I know someone who will reject you." He said: "Who?" He said: "'Awf ibn Muhallim." He said: "Come, let us go to him."

When they went and entered upon him, he said: "Welcome, O 'Amr. What brings you?" He said: "I have come to you as a suitor." He said to him: "But you are not fit for that," meaning: you are not a suitable match for marrying my daughter. 'Awf's wife heard this exchange and said to him: "O 'Awf, is this the man who came to you riding and did not stay long in conversation?"

He said: "He is 'Amr ibn Hujr, a leader of the Arabs." She said: "Why did you not host him?" meaning: entertain him and honour him. He said: "Because he insulted me." She said: "How?" He said: "He came to me as a suitor." She said: "If he is a leader of the Arabs and came to you as a suitor, whom will you marry your daughters to if not the leaders of the Arabs? Go after him and appease him."

'Awf caught up with 'Amr and his companion Ibn Sinan and called out: "O 'Amr, wait for me, and you will have from me what you desire." So 'Amr and his companion returned. 'Awf said: "You came to me while I was angry, and I said what I said. But I reconsidered myself," and he took him to the house.

'Awf had three daughters: an eldest, a middle one and a youngest. He came to the eldest and said: "O my daughter, 'Amr ibn Hujr has come to propose to you." She said: "No, Father." He said: "Why?" She said: "I am a woman with a defect in my face, meaning there is something in my face that repels the one who looks at her, and I have a harsh temper. Al-Harith is not a neighbour to you, nor am I the daughter of his paternal uncle. I fear that if something happens from me, he will divorce me, and that will become a disgrace for me." He said: "Stand up; may God bless you."

Then he went to the middle one and said to her what he had said to her sister. She said: "No, Father. I am a woman who is not beautiful, nor skilled in crafts, and I fear that he will divorce me, and that will become a disgrace for me."

He said to her: "Stand up; may God bless you."

Then he brought the youngest and said to her what he had said to her sisters. She said to him: "Yes, Father. I am good in character, beautiful in form, and skilled with my hands. If he divorces me, may God not bless him, nor grant him a successor."

'Awf went out and said to 'Amr: "I have married you to my youngest daughter, Buhaysah." Then he prepared a tent for him in his house so that he could enter upon his bride. When he entered upon her, she said to him: "I had loved you and respected you, but now I have lost interest in you." He said: "Why?" She said: "Shall this happen in my father's house and before my brothers? By God, it shall never happen."

He said: "Then let us travel to our homeland."

He ordered his companion Ibn Sinan to travel with the caravan, while he stayed behind at the side of the road and entered upon her. She said: "Is this how one treats a captive taken by force? By God, it will never be, except when you go to your tribe, slaughter, sacrifice and feed the people, and do what someone like you does for someone like me."

When he reached his tribe, he slaughtered the animals and fed the people. Then he wanted to enter upon her, but she said: "O 'Amr, do you desire women while there are two tribes in the Arabs fighting each other? Go and reconcile them first, and then nothing of your family will escape you."

'Amr went out, reconciled the two tribes, and paid the blood-money for the slain from both sides, three thousand camels from his own wealth. Then he returned to his wife. When she learned what he had done, she said to him: "Now, O al-Harith." These are examples of women who had sound reason, correct opinion and ability in argument.

When 'Umar wished to propose to Umm Unas bint 'Awf, he summoned a woman from Kindah named 'Isam, and said to her: "Go until you learn for me the knowledge concerning the daughter of 'Awf." She went to the house of 'Awf and met Umamah, and she learned from her the reason for her coming. Umamah made a tent for her daughter and said: "Sit in it, and 'Isam will enter upon you. Do not conceal from her anything she wishes to see of your face and form, and speak to her in what she asks you about, because she has come for such-and-such."

'Isam entered upon Umm Unas and found her as she wanted. She concealed nothing from her. She said: "Abandoning deception is what removes the veil," and it became a proverb among the Arabs until now.

When she returned to 'Amr, he said: "What have you brought, O 'Isam?" She said: "The churn has produced butter"—meaning the journey brought the desired result. He said: "Tell me." She said: "I will tell you the truth and sincerity." Then she began describing Umm Unas to him "from head to toe," and we will suffice here with describing what is not forbidden.

She said: "I saw a forehead like a polished mirror, adorned by hair like braided horses' tails. If you combed it you would think it chains, and if you let it down you would say: clusters of grapes washed by the heavy rain. Beneath it are two arched eyebrows, as if drawn with a pen or blackened with soot, arched over the eyes of a gazelle with wide eyes, which no hunter has frightened and no lion has startled.

Between them is a nose like the edge of a polished sword, not flattened by shortness nor elongated by length. Upon it are two cheeks like crimson on pure whiteness like pearls. There is a mouth like a ring, delightful when smiling, with bright front teeth, and within it a tongue full of eloquence. It is adorned by two red lips like roses, which draw saliva like honey. Beneath it is a neck like a silver ewer, joined to two full upper arms..." up to the end of what 'Isam said in description.

Before Umm Unas left her father's house for her husband's house, Umamah bint al-Harith did not neglect to advise her daughter with this precious counsel, which guarantees marital happiness if she adheres to it. Listen as Umamah says:

"O daughter... if advice were to be abandoned for the sake of excellence of manners, it would be abandoned for you. But it is a reminder to the heedless and an aid to the intelligent. If a woman could do without a husband because of the wealth of her parents and their great need of her, you would be the most self-sufficient of people without him. But women were created for men, and men were created for women.

O daughter... you are leaving the atmosphere from which you came out, and leaving the nest in which you grew up, for a den you have not known and a companion you have not become familiar with. So preserve for him ten qualities, which will be a treasure for you:

As for the first and second: contentment with him, good hearing and obedience to him. As for the third and fourth: attentiveness to where his eyes and nose are, so that his eye does not fall upon anything ugly from you, and his nose does not smell from you anything but the finest scent. As for the fifth and sixth: attentiveness to the time of his sleep and his food, for constant hunger is a flame, and disturbed sleep is a cause of anger. As for the seventh and eighth: guarding his wealth, and caring for his household and dependants, for the essence of wealth is good management, and of dependants is good judgement.

As for the ninth and tenth: do not disobey him in any command, and do not disclose his secret, for if you oppose his command you will provoke his anger, and if you reveal his secret you will not be safe from his treachery.

Then beware of rejoicing in front of him when he is anxious, or showing sorrow in front of him when he is joyful..." These are examples of women with sound reason and correct judgement. If wives had taken this advice, it would have spared us much of the marital discord from which we suffer today.

This is another of their claims and fabrications against Allah. This verse comes after they attributed offspring to Allah: ﴿And they have made of His servants a portion [of Him].﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 15]. Secondly, they attributed daughters to Allah and reserved sons for themselves. Allah, glorified is He, has made clear the corruption of their beliefs and refuted them with proof and evidence from their own lived reality.

Here they describe the angels, who are the servants of the All-Merciful, with femininity, and this is yet another fabrication. Allah refutes them: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 19]. That is: how can they pass this judgment upon the angels? Did they witness the creation of the angels, so that they know they are females? Then He threatens them: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 19]. It will be written down and recorded against them, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be held accountable for all these fabrications.

In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation, nor would I have taken the misleaders as helpers.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 51].

Reality has come to confirm the truth of this verse, and we have seen misleaders in every age leading people astray and turning them away from the truth, beginning with those who attributed offspring to Allah, and attributed daughters to Allah, and described the angels as females, down to those who said that man's origin is the ape and that he evolved.

We ask all of these: Did you witness the creation of Allah? The Creator, Allah, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation﴾ [Al-Kahf: 51]. So: do not believe these people, for they are liars and misleaders, and Allah, exalted is He, has subjected them to serve the truth and made them evidence of the truth of His speech.

Among these misleaders are a people who denied the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We follow only what is in the Qur'an and we do not acknowledge the Sunnah." This group came as proof of the truthfulness of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who informed of their coming fourteen centuries ago, and so he (ﷺ) said:

This is another of their claims and their fabrications against God. Therefore God refutes them: this speech is a lie and a fabrication that you utter without awareness and without knowledge. ﴿They are only conjecturing.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 20] Meaning: they are only lying in this claim.
Why do they do this? Did a messenger come to them with this claim, saying these words, or permitting them to worship idols? ﴿So they hold fast to it﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 21]. He means: firmly.

Therefore: the matter is one of blind imitation, without reflection or interpretation. They said, ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion (ummah)﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 22], meaning: upon a religion, or a creed, or a way intended by the verb (amma), meaning: to intend. ﴿And indeed, we are following in their footsteps﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 22], upon their way, ﴿guided﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 22], meaning: this way is the one that shows us and guides us.

The Noble Qur'an addressed this matter in detail in other places. In one verse He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 170].

And in another verse He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 104].

Consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression in these two verses, and how each verse is concluded with what suits it. First, you find that the general meaning of the two verses is one, but in the first they said: ﴿Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 170], and in the other they said: ﴿Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 104].

They used the style of restriction and confinement (qasr wa hasr), restricting their worship to what they found their fathers upon. So the aversion in this one is stronger than in the first, and therefore the end of the verse came with what suits their aversion.

In the first, the Exalted said in response to them, with this exclamatory interrogation: ﴿Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 170], and in the other He said: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 104]. So what is the difference between ﴿they understand (ya'qiluna)﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 170] and ﴿they know (ya'lamuna)﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 104]? "Ya'qiluna" means: one who derives matters by himself, through his own mind; whereas "ya'lamuna" means: one who is not able to derive, but knows only from what another has derived.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verse 23:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a warner (nadhir)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. He means: a messenger. No messenger was ever sent except that he was met with this denial and this obstinacy ﴿except that its affluent ones (mutrafun) said﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. The mutrafun are those who are pampered and immersed in desires, and they are always the leaders of disbelief and the leaders in denying the messengers. ﴿"Upon a community"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23], meaning upon a creed or upon a way. ﴿"And indeed we are following their footsteps"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. He means: we travel and proceed along exactly their path.
This indicates their determination to turn away and their clinging to the misguidance in which they and their fathers were.

Because this is God's way with the messengers, and with everyone who denies the messengers: ﴿Indeed, Our word had already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers, they would be the victorious﴾ [As-Saffat: 171-173].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, brings what undermines this process of imitation (taqlid, blind adherence to what one's forebears did) and nullifies it, and exposes their falsehood in it. So He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And when Abraham said...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verse 26:

Almighty God wishes to expose their falsehood and unmask their lie in their saying, ﴿Nay, we follow what we found our fathers doing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170], and to present to them a real-life proof drawn from their own lives. Here is our master Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), father of the prophets, the focus of the gaze of all the Arabs, who sanctify him and take pride in being connected to him.

They say: "We are of the lineage of Abraham, and Abraham did not imitate his father in worshipping idols, so why do you imitate your fathers and not Abraham?"

Almighty God refutes the matter of imitation (taqlid) in practice, through the story of our master Abraham, and refutes it philosophically too. For if you trace existence back to its beginning, you will find only Adam, peace be upon him. Adam came with a method (manhaj), followed it, and his children after him followed it. So how did deviation from this method occur?

Therefore, there must have arisen, over the passage of time, people who departed from the method and inverted the realities out of desires within themselves. Among these came a generation that worshipped idols, because they were not governed by the method of heaven nor by the matter of obligations (takalif): "Do" and "do not." So the worship of gods that have no obligation attached to them suited them, and therefore they worshipped idols.

As for His saying, ﴿And when Abraham said to his father﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 26], it has been the subject of wide debate among scholars: is he his real father, or is he his paternal uncle Azar? One who traces the word (abihi, "his father") in the Qur'an finds that it occurs eight times, the first in surah al-An'am, ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾ [al-An'am: 74], and the last in surah al-Mumtahanah. The phrase (li-abihi) does not come again after that except once, in the story of our master Joseph: ﴿When Joseph said to his father﴾ [Yusuf: 4].

Therefore, the name Azar appears only in the verse of al-An'am, which is the first of the eight occurrences, as though God, may He be exalted, has settled the dispute on this matter. He wished to make clear to us that Azar was his uncle, by the evidence that He said ﴿to his father Azar﴾ [al-An'am: 74], and in the remaining places He said (li-abihi), meaning: the one you already know, namely in surah al-An'am.

This is a common usage in our language: we call an uncle "father." When a man asks, "Is your father present?" you understand that he means the real father. But if he says to you, "Is your father Muhammad present?", he means your uncle, because he specified him by a proper name after the descriptive term.

The Qur'an also includes the paternal uncle among the fathers, in His saying, ﴿Or were you witnesses when death came to Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

The word ﴿fathers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133] is a plural that includes Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac. When a plural is taken in the sense of a plural, the division is singular: you take "a father who is Abraham, a father who is Ishmael, a father who is Isaac." These three are fathers of Jacob. Ishmael was the brother of Isaac, and if Ishmael was a father, then Isaac is not a father but an uncle. Therefore the uncle was called a father.

Thus, in the first verse that speaks of our master Abraham, Almighty God mentioned ﴿to his father Azar﴾ [al-An'am: 74] to show that Azar, whom Abraham argued with and debated over the matter of monotheism, was not Abraham's real father, but his uncle.

We find evidence for this in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), where he said, in the hadith about his own lineage (ﷺ), that the genealogical chain of the Prophet (ﷺ) leads to his father Abraham. It is therefore not valid that the father of Abraham was an unbeliever worshipping idols.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed I am innocent (bara'un) of what you worship﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 26]: bara'un means the same as bari' (innocent, free of). The difference between them is that bara' is said of the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine, whereas bari' is inflected for the dual and plural and for gender. In another place He described them as enemies: ﴿Indeed they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 77], meaning the idols. So, as long as the matter involves associating partners with God or disbelief in Allah, I disassociate myself from it.

Meaning of ﴿fa-taranī﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 27]: He created me and originated me. ﴿Fa-innahu sa-yahdīni﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 27]: this indicates that the method must come from the One who created, for it is He who sets the method, and He who guides. It is not valid that God creates while people set the method.

As we said in the matter of the Maker who sets a "catalogue" (manual) for the maintenance of His creation, because He is the most knowledgeable of it, the expert in what sets it right.

Here He said ﴿fa-innahu sa-yahdīni﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 27], with the sīn (sa-), which indicates the future, and in another place He said ﴿fa-huwa yahdīni﴾ [al-Shu'arā': 78], in the present tense, and this indicates that guidance from God is continuous in the present and the future.

And because guidance and the method can only come from the One who created, He used the restrictive construction (qaṣr): ﴿fa-innahu sa-yahdīni﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 27], and in the verse of al-Shu'arā': ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me. And who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ [al-Shu'arā': 78-80].

He placed the detached pronoun before the verb to indicate that the action is restricted to God Most High, because these actions have an appearance of being shared with God. As for actions that belong to God alone, in which there is no possibility of partnership, they come without restriction: ﴿Who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾ [al-Shu'arā': 81].

﴿وَجَعَلَهَا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 28]: that is, our master Abraham made it the word of disavowal of polytheism (kalimat al-bara'a min al-shirk), or the word of tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), which appears in His saying: ﴿And Abraham charged his sons with it, and Jacob too: "O my sons, God has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims."﴾ [al-Baqara: 132].

He made this word ﴿remaining﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 28], continuing ﴿among his descendants﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 28], that is, among his offspring after him. This word has remained lasting and circulating on the tongues of people until the Day of Resurrection, because it is a good word, and God, glorified is He, guaranteed its permanence in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how God sets forth a parable: a good word like a good tree, its root firm and its branches in the sky, giving its fruit every season by the permission of its Lord?﴾ [Ibrahim: 24-25].

He called it a "word" (kalima) although it is speech (kalam), because in the language the word kalima is used for speech, as we say: "So-and-so delivered a word (kalima) at the gathering." And Ibn Malik (Ibn Malik) says in his Alfiyya:

"And kalima is that by which speech is meant."

That is, by "word" we mean a great deal of speech.

We said: the method (manhaj) gets obliterated, and people turn away from it as time passes, until the need arises for a new prophet who restores people to the right path. This is because the Real, glorified is He, created in the human soul a natural immunity, since he is God's vicegerent (khalifah) on His earth. He is the one who will populate this earth, so he must be provided with the means of uprightness and of the positive movement by which he populates the earth.

Therefore, we see that the sound human being, when he commits a sin out of heedlessness of his Lord's method, hastens to repentance and remorse, because uprightness and the seed of faith are within his very self. But if a person is afflicted in himself and loses this immunity, immunity comes from society: the conscious society that is aware of its collective role in enjoining good and forbidding evil. If society too loses this immunity, nothing remains but for heaven to intervene with a new messenger and a new method.

So: the turning away from the method occurred after Ibrahim and Isma'il, and so the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) came. Our master Ibrahim made the word of tawhid (monotheism) remain among his descendants, ﴿so that they might return﴾, i.e., his descendants after him, [might return] to God.

But it did not happen. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Nay, but I gave enjoyment to these, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴾and their fathers﴿ with status, authority, luxury and security. ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67]. He gave them a rank and sanctity among the Arabs because of their station with respect to the House, and this rank remained for them ﴿until there came to them the Truth﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and a clear Messenger﴾, i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Clear﴾ means: he makes the truth manifest through his hands and in everything in it.

But did they believe in this truth and affirm this Messenger? No.

The method (al-manhaj) becomes obscured, and people turn away from it as time passes, until the need arises for a new prophet to bring people back to the right path (al-jadda). This is because God, glory be to Him, placed in the human soul a natural immunity, since man is God's vicegerent on His earth. He is the one who will populate this earth, so he must be provided with the means of uprightness and the positive activity by which he builds the earth.

Thus we see that the sound person, when he commits a sin in a moment of heedlessness toward the method of his Lord, hastens to repentance and remorse, because uprightness and the seed of faith are within him. But if a person is afflicted in himself and loses this immunity, immunity comes from society: a conscious society aware of its collective role in enjoining good and forbidding evil. If society too loses this immunity, nothing remains but for heaven to intervene with a new messenger and a new method.

Therefore, the turning away from the method occurred after Ibrahim and Isma'il, and so came the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). Our master Ibrahim made the word of monotheism remain in his descendants, ﴿so that they might return﴾ [43:28], that is, his offspring after him, ﴿return﴾ [43:28], that is, to God.

But it did not happen. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ [43:29], that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿and their fathers﴾ [43:29], with status, authority, luxury and security. ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [29:67], and He gave them a station and sanctity among the Arabs because of their place with respect to the House. This station remained theirs ﴿until there came to them the truth﴾ [43:29], that is, the Qur'an, ﴿and a clear messenger﴾ [43:29], that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). The word ﴿clear﴾ [43:29] means that the truth is made manifest through his hands and in everything about him.

But did they believe in this truth and affirm this messenger? No. ﴿And when the truth came to them, they said: "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾ [43:30], that is, they said the Qur'an is magic that bewitches whoever hears it, and in another place they said about the Messenger that he is a magician.

We have said that refuting this fabrication is easy. If the Qur'an were magic, and if Muhammad were a magician who bewitched the believers in him, then why did he not bewitch you too, and the matter would end? Therefore, your being upon disbelief is proof of Muhammad's truthfulness, and that he is a prophet, not a magician.

When this doubt failed to succeed, they said: ﴿Only a human teaches him﴾ [16:103], that is, the Messenger of God goes to a Persian man who teaches him the Qur'an. God responded to them: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [16:103].

They said about him (ﷺ) that he is mad, so God responded to them: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed you are upon a great moral character﴾ [68:2–4]. A madman cannot be a person of great character, because character regulates the conduct of its possessor.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, had nullified their claims and fabrications, and answered them in a way that exposed their foolishness, they said:

﴿And they said, "Why was this not sent down...﴾.

This is an acknowledgment from them that the Qur'an is true and that there is no objection to it. Their objection is only to the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he was of ordinary standing among the people and not one of their great figures, nor one of their chiefs, in the two towns, that is, Makkah and al-Ta'if. In al-Ta'if there was 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, and in Makkah al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, along with others. So Allah responded to them: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾....

Meaning: If We have divided between them the most basic things, which are their livelihoods in the life of this world, would they themselves wish to divide the mercy of Allah and the bounty of Allah according to their own whims? The mercy of Allah is specific to whomever He wills of His servants. It is in His hand, glorified is He, and no one has any share in its distribution.

So the words of the Exalted: ﴿We have apportioned between them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank﴾ indicate the helplessness of man, and that the movement of life is not set right except by the method of Allah that organizes it.

Among the wisdom of this division is that He made some people rich and others poor, some of them leaders and others servants. Had it not been for this division, the movement of society would not have been upright, and we would not find anyone to carry out the arduous work or the menial work.

We have already explained that the movement of society and its progress do not rest on generosity but on need, for the need of the poor is what drives him to work.

The mercy intended here, ﴿Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾, is prophethood. They covet that it become a choice they make from among their leaders and the great men of their people. So the Truth, glorified is He, corrects them and says: How do you aspire to that when you cannot even apportion the most basic things?

Then you notice that the phrase ﴿and raised some of them above others in rank﴾ is an indefinite phrase meaning that everyone is both elevated and elevated over: elevated in one matter, and elevated over in another matter.

Thus creation is complemented, interests are fulfilled, and the needs of society are met, as the poet said:

You are elevated in what you do well from among the deeds, and you are elevated over in what you do not excel at. This is the meaning of His words, the Exalted: ﴿that some of them may take others in service﴾.

﴿But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ The mercy of your Lord here means the message and the method that guides creation to the path of truth. This mercy is in reality better than this fleeting provision for which you compete in this world, because man, however far he reaches in this world in luxury, opulence and comfort, will die and leave it, and nothing of it will remain for him.

As for the method of Allah, it bequeaths to you an enduring success by which you are made happy in this world and triumphant in the Hereafter. So: it is better and more lasting, and it is more beneficial to you and more enduring. This method guarantees for you the goodness of this world and the safety of the Hereafter; therefore it is better than everything you see of the glitter of this world.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verses 33–35:

The meaning of ﴿a single community﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33] is: upon one religion, united in disbelief. Had it not been that people would see the disbelievers living in luxury and be tempted by them, I would have given them all this abundance, such that no one would be superior to them, because this abundance is the abundance of this world, which ends with its end and does not last. Although the world is for the reckoning of the disbelievers, the Hereafter is for the God-fearing.

Here the Qur'an speaks of the advancements of mankind that they came to know after fourteen centuries from the revelation of the Qur'an. So "ma'arij" means: the elevators or staircases upon which one ascends, ﴿and staircases upon which they climb﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33], meaning: they ascend and rise.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is belittling the matter of the disbelievers' luxury, so that we are not deceived by them, nor wish for what they have of fleeting adornment.

After that, He shows us that those who live in luxury and affluence will reach a time when they love to return to the original source and to the simplicity of nature. You see them, for example, at the end of the week going out into the open countryside and throwing themselves into the bosom of nature, eating what the earth produces and living on the bare minimum. Why? Because they have grown weary of the life of excessive comfort; they have grown weary of the life of civilization and its defects and negatives.

Meaning of: "And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the All-Merciful" — i.e., he turns away from it, or feigns blindness to it and neglects it. Because he has neglected something of great importance that he should not neglect or turn away from, Allah punishes him: ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾ — We prepare for him and make ready for him a devil, ﴿and he becomes his companion﴾ — i.e., he is constantly with him, misleading him and whispering to him.

We said: Because the Truth, glory be to Him, is independent of His creation, and He is the Lord of the believer and the Lord of the disbeliever. Therefore He helps each one in what he wills: whoever wants guidance, He helps him toward it and increases him in it; and whoever wants disbelief, He seals upon his heart so that no faith enters it and no disbelief leaves it. Therefore He brings here the attribute (al-Rahman).

Therefore the devil most often comes to a person at the time of prayer, to corrupt his relationship with his Lord...
