Then ﴿They will not be relieved of it﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 75], meaning: it will not be lightened for them; ﴿and they will be in it despairing﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 75], meaning: they will be full of anguish and despondent about deliverance, despairing of good, with no hope in their hearts of ever leaving it. Thus He has gathered upon them every aspect of pain, anguish, despair and the severing of hope.

Because what they have come to in terms of punishment is the recompense of their deeds, and it is not an injustice to them, since We guided them and made clear to them good and evil: ﴿And We showed him the two paths﴾ [Al-Balad: 10]. And He said: ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [Ash-Shams: 8]. Yet they wronged themselves when they hastened to seize their desires for themselves, and took hold of them in what is forbidden, so Allah deprived them of the lawful enjoyment that is everlasting in the Hereafter. The worst injustice is that a person wrongs himself, and wronging oneself is folly and transgression.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verses 77–78:

The discussion here concerns the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us. They call out to Malik, the keeper of the Fire: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 77], meaning: by death, so that we may rest from what we are in of the constant torment that never ends. For the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [al-Nisa: 56].

We have said that modern sciences have established that the skin is the seat of sensation, as evidence of which, when you take an injection, for example, you feel the pain only to the extent that the needle penetrates the skin. The Qur'an has preceded all the sciences in explaining this fact. Therefore the people of the Fire seek death to rescue them from this punishment.

However, we notice that the verb ﴿li-yaqdi﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 77] came in the imperative form and was also accompanied by the imperative lam (lam al-amr, the lam of command). Is the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, then commanded, especially by the people of the Fire? We say: if the request comes from one above to one below, it is a command (amr); if it comes from an equal, it is an entreaty (iltimas); and if it comes from one below to one above, it is a supplication (du'a'). So we do not command Allah; rather, we supplicate Him.

(He) said, that is Malik: ﴿Indeed, you will remain﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 77], remaining in the Fire, abiding in it forever, for you have no excuse. ﴿We certainly brought you the truth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 78], that is: the true religion and the true method. ﴿But most of you are averse to the truth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 78]. This is the meaning of ﴿We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 76].

Then the context turns the discourse to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His Lord often addresses him to console him and lighten his burden, for he encountered much of the harshness and obstinacy of his people, and they harmed him in his person and body when they incited their foolish ones against him, pelted him with stones until his feet bled, and threw the entrails of a camel and filth onto his back while he was praying.

They also harmed him in his moral standing: they called him a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a liar, a poet, and a madman. So the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear to him that he came after a gap between the messengers, after creation had become corrupt and evil had spread. Behind this corruption are people who profit from it and defend it, and it is natural that they would confront you and stand against your call, for they want to preserve their position and their gains from this corruption.

The hatred of these people toward the Messenger of Allah reached the point that they plotted to kill him and be rid of his call. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when those who disbelieve plot against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you; they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

﴿Or have they determined a matter...﴾.

﴿Or have they determined a matter...﴾.

It means: they have firmly planned a scheme against you, O Muhammad, and plotted it and agreed upon it, so do not be concerned, for We are watching them closely. ﴿Then, verily, We are the ones who firmly plan.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 79] That is, We firmly plan a scheme just as they have firmly planned one. We know what they plot in secret, and it is not hidden from Us, while they do not know what We plot against them. So then: which of the two parties is stronger?

Do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Indeed, We do; and Our messengers are with them, recording.

Do they think that We do not hear their secret (sirr) and their private conspiracy, what they plot and carefully devise to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? And We do not hear their secret. The sirr (secret) is the talk you share with another in confidence, or the secret that, when you have heard something and it stays hidden in your breast, no one else is aware of it.

And the najwa (private consultation) is the low-voiced talk between two people such that no third person can hear them. But Allah hears their secret and hears their najwa, and nothing about their affair is hidden from Him. Moreover, ﴿And Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 80], meaning: We hear them and We record upon them what they say. So We have messengers and angels who write down and register what they say and what they do.

So if you say: if Allah, glorified is He, knows and hears, and nothing about their affair is hidden from Him, what is the benefit of recording against them and writing down their secret and their private talk?

We say: the writing benefits the angels, and it is for their sake. So that when they see the events occurring just as they were recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), they know that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and so their certainty increases upon their certainty, and their faith upon their faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 43, verse 81:

This is a command to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): (Say) "O Muhammad," to the one who claims that the All-Merciful has a son. ﴿Say﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 81], meaning by way of supposition.

﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of those who worship [him]﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 81]. On the reading that (in) is conditional, the meaning is: if the All-Merciful had a son, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who informs me of this reality, then I would be the first to worship Him, because I take my culture and my commands from my Lord, not from you.

Some of them said that (in) here is negative, like the words of the Exalted: ﴿Their mothers are not they, their mothers are only those who gave birth to them﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 2]. So the meaning is: "Say: there was never a son for the All-Merciful, and I am the first to deny that, because I am the first of those who worship [Him], and the first of those who believe in the oneness of God, the Exalted."

The Truth, the Exalted, described Himself, glory be to Him, with two attributes. Some think they have one meaning, but since they are two different words, each must have a particular meaning that the other attribute does not convey. The Truth described Himself as "One" (Wahid) and "Unique" (Ahad).

We have said: "Wahid" means a single being with no second, so it negates plurality. As for "Ahad," it means one in His essence, with no parts, because a thing composed of parts is such that each part depends on the other parts.

Since He, the Exalted, is Ahad in His essence, He therefore has no son, because a son is a part of his father. In the noble hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, meaning: "[Fatimah] is a part of me."

If we apply this principle and trace the lineage of each of us, we must arrive at our father Adam (peace be upon him). We know that each of us contains a portion or an atom of our father Adam. This atom is the one that witnessed the first covenant that Allah, the Exalted, took from the children of Adam while they were in the stage of the atoms: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying]: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"* Or [lest] you say, "Our fathers had associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] offspring after them. Then would You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172–173].

This atom is the seed of goodness and the locus of faith in man, and from it the movement of goodness proceeds. Do you not see that he regrets sin and resolves to repent? It is the work of this atom and its effect on the human soul, because it was the first to hear the call of Allah and is a message from Allah.

The Noble Qur'an indicates that the jinn are more perceptive than humans regarding this matter. If man has dared against the Truth, the Exalted, and attributed a son to Him, then the jinn have denied that and declared Allah free of having a son or a consort. Read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And [it is] that He—exalted is the majesty of our Lord—has not taken a consort or a son﴾ [Al-Jinn: 3].

That is, from His greatness, the Exalted, He has taken neither a consort (meaning a wife) nor a son. The one who reflects finds that the consort and the son are among the causes of corruption in the universe. The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ [At-Taghabun: 14].

We say, for example, in the customs of people: "Marry early so that you may have a child to support you in your old age." But does the Truth, glory be to Him, take a son because He needs one as we need one? Then, those who said that Jesus is the son of Allah, what is their position regarding the time before Jesus? Was there not a son of Allah then? And as for after Jesus, where is the son that Allah has taken? So, all of this is a fabrication against Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 43, verse 82:

It is appropriate that this verse begin with the word ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 82], after the discussion in the preceding verse about negating offspring from God, the Exalted. The word (subhan, "glory be to") means: declaring God, the Exalted, far above everything that may occur to your mind.

Therefore the phrase subhan Allah ("glory be to God") is never used except in conjunction with something wondrous beyond the grasp of human reason: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36]. ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque﴾ [al-Isra': 1].

That is to say: when your minds stop at such matters, say "Glory be to God," and declare God free of any resemblance to creation. Do not measure His strength by your strength, nor His action by your action, nor His power by your power. Declare God free of any likeness in His names, in His attributes, and in His actions.

Then reflect on how, in this verse, the Truth, glorified is He, brings attributes that suit the negation of offspring from Him. He says ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 82]. Does the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them have need of a child? In another verse He says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

Greater than the heavens and the earth is the Throne (Lord of the Throne). Thus He, glorified is He, is free of need to take a child. His saying ﴿of what they describe﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 82] means: of what they lie about, or of what they ascribe to God by way of taking a child.

We have said that the glorification of God continues throughout all time and is established for God before time, for God is exalted, and this is an essential attribute in Him, glorified is He, before He created those who glorify Him. So the word (subhan) is essential to God before He created creation. When He brought this universe into being, the universe glorified God: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies God﴾ [al-Hashr: 1].

This glorification continues in the present and the future: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him﴾ [al-Hashr: 24]. And since the universe is a single system glorifying God, the Exalted, O human, do not deviate from this system; be glorifying as well: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1].

This is a command to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿So leave them﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83]. Leave them, O Muhammad, to plunge into this false talk they are engaged in. The word ﴿yakhuḍū﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83] comes from al-khawḍ (plunging). Its original sense is a person wading into the deep waters of a great sea, and then it was used figuratively for one who engages in talk without knowledge.

Its most common use is for false talk. Al-khawḍ suggests floundering and walking in unknown places where you do not know what dangers may confront you there, so you become the one who harms himself. Therefore: you must scrutinize before you plunge in, and beware of plunging into falsehood.

As for His words ﴿and play﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83]: because I commanded them to be earnest in life, yet they are playing in it. Seriousness (jadd) is opposed by idle amusement (lahw) and play (la'b). The difference between lahw and la'b is that la'b is doing something with no benefit except entertainment, and this is before the age of obligation (taklīf). If a person is responsible (mukallaf) and does what has no benefit, then it is lahw.

From this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿But when they saw a trade or a diversion, they dispersed to it and left you standing﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 11]. So lahw is to be occupied with play that benefits nothing, instead of a duty that has been required of you.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83]. So Allah has warned them (awʿadahum) of this Day; He did not leave them neglected, nor did He create them in vain. Rather, He made clear to them truth and falsehood, and promised them recompense, each according to what he deserves. The verb ﴿yūʿadūn﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83] is from awʿada (to threaten/warn), which is warning of evil before its time so that you may avoid it.

There is also wa'd (promise), and a promise is only ever of good.

So: those who enter the Fire, Allah has not wronged them, nor seized them unawares; rather He warned them and cautioned them about this destination. The Qur'an is full of promise and warning. Read: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah] and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward difficulty﴾ [Al-Layl: 5–10].

So the Exalted Lord has offered His servant good both in His promise and in His warning. Indeed, even the warning contains good, because the one who cautions you against evil before you fall into it has done you a favor that deserves your gratitude.

In light of this we understand His words, Exalted is He, as He enumerates His blessings upon us in Surat ar-Rahman: ﴿There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 35–36]. Can fire, flame and brass be counted among the blessings of Allah? Yes, it is a blessing from Allah, because He warns you of the causes of falling into it and keeps you far from it.

Thus the verse ﴿So leave them to plunge and play until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 83] is a call to the Messenger of Allah to make the matter easy on himself and not to burden himself because of the obstinacy of his people and their persistence in misguidance.

So the Exalted Lord consoles His Messenger and lightens his burden, as He addressed him in many verses with this meaning, such as His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿So let not your soul depart [in pursuit] of them in regret. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ [Fatir: 8].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 84:

Some people imagine that Allah, exalted is He, is in the heaven, so that when they call upon Him they raise their voices so that He may hear them. Allah, glorified is He, is in every place and at every time. He has no place that contains Him and no time that encompasses Him, because He, glorified is He, is the Creator of time and the Creator of place, and the created cannot contain the Creator.

Therefore we do not use "where" (ayna) or "when" (matā) with regard to Allah. ﴿He it is who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. So He is in every place. This attribute (ilah, "God") is essential to Him, glorified is He; it is an attribute of perfection that never leaves Him or separates from Him, neither in the heaven nor in the earth.

The orientalists paused at this verse because of the repetition of the indefinite noun, ﴿He it is who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. The word (ilah, "God") is indefinite and it is repeated. The linguistic rule is that when an indefinite noun is repeated, the second is other than the first, as when you say: "I met a man (rajulan), and I honoured a man (rajulan)," so the second "man" is other than the first.

As for a definite noun when it is repeated, the second is the very same as the first, if you say: "I met the man (al-rajul), and I honoured the man (al-rajul)," so: it is the same man. This rule places us in a difficulty with this verse, for who would say there is one god in the heaven and another god in the earth?!

The saying of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), confirms this rule, for when he recited: ﴿So indeed with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 5-6], he said: "Hardship (al-'usr) came definite, and ease (yusr) came indefinite."

There is a story connected with this verse involving the dervishes in the Ahmadi Mosque in Tanta. One day Sheikh Mahmud Shaltut, who was Sheikh of al-Azhar, came to visit the city of Tanta, and he came to the Ahmadi Mosque to pray. After the prayer, Sheikh Abu al-'Uyun, who was a professor of tafsir, asked him, saying: "Praise be to God, O our master, that I found you here, for in the tafsir lesson yesterday I stood before the verse: ﴿He it is who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84], and the rule is that when an indefinite noun is repeated, the second is other than the first?"

As soon as Sheikh Shaltut began to answer and said: "By God, the scholars have said the rule is a general majority," a man whom we did not know before and did not know afterward entered. He was bareheaded and held a staff in his hand, and he said: "O scholars, you have forgotten the relative pronoun ﴿He it is who (huwa alladhi)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. The relative pronoun is definite, and what follows it is its relative clause. So the repeated word is a relative clause of a single relative pronoun, meaning it is the very same." Then the man left, and we sat without any of us speaking for half an hour.

As for His saying: ﴿and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. Al-Hakim (the All-Wise) is He who places a thing in its proper place with wisdom. Al-'Alim (the All-Knowing) is He who knows what sets right His creation and what helps them in their livelihood and in their final return. He, glorified is He, would not give them the foundations of material existence in food, drink and air and then leave them without a method and without values that nourish their spirits as He nourished their bodies.

For this reason He named this method a "spirit" (ruh). It is to the heart what the spirit is to the bodies. The difference between the two spirits is that the spirit in the body has an appointed time when it departs the body by death, whereas the spirit of values and method is lasting and eternal; it accompanies a person in this world and goes with him into the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 85:

The word ﴿wa-tabaraka﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 85] is a fixed word (kalimah jamidah) with no derivation (ishtiqaq) in it. It means: exalted is His station, and abundant is His giving. "Tabaraka" derives from al-barakah (blessing), meaning abundance of good, in that He gives you a little which becomes much, more than you were expecting.

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 85]. In another verse He said: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [Al-Hajj: 64], meaning: to Him belongs the container and the contained.

In Surah Ta-Ha He said, glorified is He: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil﴾ [Ta-Ha: 6].

Thus the verses have encompassed the whole of existence and made it a dominion belonging to Allah, Exalted is He: the entire cosmos with its heavens and its earth, what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, what is between the heavens and the earth, and what is beneath the earth, all of it is the dominion of Allah.

Finally, we have learned that all good is buried beneath the soil (al-tharā), which Allah reveals to His servants when He wills, in accordance with the development of their life and its advancement. In the depths of the earth now there is water, petroleum, minerals, precious stones and valuable things.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, by His saying ﴿and what is beneath the soil﴾ [Ta-Ha: 6] is alerting us to give attention to the interior of the earth, to digging into it, and to searching it in order to extract its good things.

Therefore we see geologists, paleontologists and petroleum scientists traversing the lands from one end to the other in search of these good things, even in the seas, because these fall within this meaning, for they are from the earth, even though they represent three-quarters of the earth.

Then comes His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 85]. Thus, in the style of restriction (qasr) in both places, He placed the prepositional phrase first to convey that knowledge of the Hour is restricted to Allah alone, to the exclusion of any other.

Likewise, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 85]: to Him alone, to no other. You will not be returned except to Him. It is as if it were a concise message to the human being: remember your end and your afterlife, remember the recompense for deeds, and do not let blessings deceive you, for after them there is reckoning and recompense. ﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, because he sees himself self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [Al-Alaq: 6-8]. So everything is from Allah and to Allah: from Allah in creation, provision and nurture, and to Allah in return and final resort.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 86:

Meaning: those whom they invoke besides Allah, such as the sun, the moon, the stars and idols. These objects of worship are false objects of worship, as evidenced by the fact that they possess no intercession and cannot remove harm from those who worship them. They possess no intercession because intercession belongs to whom? To Allah.

And how would Allah accept their intercession, when they are the cause of these people's misguidance? ﴿Except for those who bear witness to the truth, and they know﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 86]. This is an exception: meaning, no one intercedes with Allah except those who bear witness to the truth.

Then: these people believe and acknowledge that Allah is their Creator. And in another verse: ﴿If you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?", they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 61]. It is strange of them that, after this acknowledgment, they do not believe in Allah or accept His Messenger.

Therefore He concluded the verse with His saying, ﴿how are they turned away?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87]: how are they diverted from this truth while they acknowledge it and bear witness before Allah that He is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth?

Therefore, in Surah al-Baqarah, the Truth, glory be to Him, marvels at their disbelief, which has no justification and no grounds. He says, Exalted is He: ﴿How do you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life again, then to Him you will be returned?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 88:

The word (qīlihi) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) of qāla (to say). We say qāla qawlan, maqālan, and qīlan, so the meaning of (qīlihi) is qawlihi (his saying). Whose saying? The saying of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), addressing his Lord: ﴿O my Lord, these are a people who will not believe﴾. These are the disbelievers of Makkah.

Notice that the Prophet (ﷺ) was harmed by these people in his person and in his morale, by being accused of what was not in him: sorcery, poetry, soothsaying and madness; and in his family. He suffered the utmost hardship from them. Yet he mentioned nothing of all this. The only thing he cared about was the matter of the people's faith. He did not say, "O Lord, my people have harmed me and done such and such"; rather he said, ﴿O my Lord, these are a people who will not believe﴾.

This is what stung him and angered him (ﷺ). It is established in the authentic hadith that the Prophet (ﷺ) never took revenge for himself, and never became angry for his own sake. His jealousy and his anger were only for Allah, and for the truth with which he came and to which he called people...

As for the meaning of the wāw at the beginning of the verse (wa-qīlihi): this wāw carries the sense of an oath. It is as if the Exalted Lord swears by the saying of the Messenger of Allah, ﴿O my Lord, these are a people who will not believe﴾, meaning: by the truth of this saying.

The answer to the oath is omitted here because it is known, meaning: "I will surely punish them with a punishment that will heal your heart from them. So do not be concerned about their not believing. Had you wished, I would have compelled them to faith and made them into the likeness of angels. Your only duty, O Muhammad, is to pardon them."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 43, verse 89:

﴿So turn away from them and say, "Peace."﴾

Because turning away from them will draw them toward the courtyard of faith in you, and some of these will become soldiers among the soldiers of Islam. Indeed, we have seen Khalid ibn al-Walid, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Amr ibn al-As and others among the champions of disbelief become leaders in the ranks of the Muslims...

As for His saying, ﴿and say, "Peace"﴾, the implied meaning is: say to them, "Peace be upon you." We understand from this that the word (salam) on its own, without (alayka), is said to one with whom you have a dispute and from whom you wish to part. We say it in the reality of our lives when you disagree with another person and do not reach a resolution with him; you say to him, "Salam." Therefore, our master Ibrahim, in his argument with his father, said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾ [Maryam: 47], meaning: a farewell and a parting peace, not a peace of greeting.

As for His saying, ﴿but they will come to know﴾, it means: when you do this, they will come to know the outcome of what you have said, and they will come to know how I will punish them for their denial of you.
